$comment: VENDORED copy of the normative kiosk.tech schema at spec/schemas/pow.schema.json. This file is self-contained (no cross-file $ref). Keeping it in sync with the upstream normative copy is tracked as T-045.
title: Kiosk proof-of-work
description: The PoW challenge object (issued in a pow_required 402) and the proof(s) an agent returns in the Kiosk-PoW request header (raw JSON) on retry.

challenge.description: A single stateless, request-bound PoW challenge.

salt.description: Base64 random salt; no amortization across challenges.

exp.description: Unix expiry; scales with the number of requested proofs.

sig.description: HMAC-SHA256 over the challenge fields plus a fingerprint of the exact request.

proof.description: One solved challenge: the challenge echoed back verbatim plus its solution.

indices.description: u64 indices in Zcash canonical (subtree/tree) order; NOT a global ascending sort.

items.$comment: The upper bound is stated as an INCLUSIVE `maximum` of 2**64-1, not as `exclusiveMaximum: 2**64`. A JSON parser that reads numbers as IEEE-754 doubles rounds the largest LEGAL index, 18446744073709551615, up to exactly 2**64 -- an exclusive bound at 2**64 then REFUSES a proof the reference verifier accepts, and a bound that is wrong in the direction of rejecting valid work is the worse failure. An inclusive bound at the largest legal value survives that round-trip. The residual cost, which no JSON Schema can remove, is that such a parser also admits the handful of values between 2**64 and the next representable double; a parser with exact integers admits none of them, and the verifier refuses them all either way.

header_nonce.$comment: The bound is stated as an INCLUSIVE `maximum` of 2**32-1, matching how `indices` states its own: 4294967295 is exactly representable as an IEEE-754 double, so it survives any JSON parser, and an inclusive bound never refuses the largest legal value. Without a bound the field is unbounded on the wire while both specs call it a u32 -- and the reference verifier folds it in with `pack("V")`, which truncates mod 2**32 instead of raising, so 0, 2**32 and -(2**32) seed identically and one proof has infinitely many spellings. The verifier rejects out-of-range values for the same reason; schema and verifier state one bound, not two.
header_nonce.description: OPTIONAL u32, default 0. Folded into the PoW seed after the salt bytes as a little-endian u32; an extensibility point (currently always 0). A verifier reconstructs the seed as salt-bytes || header_nonce(LE u32), so a proof solved for a non-zero header_nonce MUST carry it.

powHeader.description: The value of the Kiosk-PoW request header, as raw JSON. Either a single proof object, or a JSON array of proofs for the N-proof case. A server also accepts repeated Kiosk-PoW header lines (one proof each) and a proxy comma-combined value; those presentations flatten to the same proofs list and are not expressed here (they are a transport concern).
